name: The confederated States and their components

arts.name: Composition of the Confederation

Each State is designated by a code made up of two letters and a number. Numbers below ninety designate territorial States; numbers ninety-one to ninety-four designate confederal territories; numbers ninety-five and ninety-six designate confederal autonomous municipalities.
Each territorial State belongs to the constituent people indicated in the list above. The confederal territories belong to no people.

arts.name: Confederal capitals
u: The institutions of the Confederation are distributed among four capitals:

Sarajevo — political capital. Seat of the Kongres, the Narodni Sabor, the Konfederalno Veće, the Confederal Chancellery and the Konfederalna Obavěštajna Agencija. Sarajevo is the official capital of the Confederation and the residence of the Confederal Council.

Beograd — economic and financial capital. Seat of the Confederal Central Bank, the Confederal Stock Exchange, the Confederal Chamber of Commerce and the Confederal Department of Finance and the Treasury.

Zagreb — judicial capital. Seat of the Ustavni Sud (Constitutional Court), the Confederal Court of Justice, the Confederal Prosecutor's Office and the Confederal Department of Justice and Fundamental Rights.

Sofija — capital of defence and sciences. Seat of the General Headquarters of the confederal armed forces, the Confederal Military Academy, the Confederal Academy of Sciences and the Confederal Department of Defence and Security. Sofija also hosts the seat of the Balkan Training Area (EBF).
The following also have their seat: in Ļubļana, the Confederal Court of Audit; in Ohrid, the Confederal Language Institute; in Cetiñe, the Confederal Library and Archives.
No major confederal institution may be concentrated in a single city. Confederal law may assign secondary institutions to other cities of the Confederation.
Sessions of the Kongres may be held in any confederal territory by decision of the Konfederalno Veće.

arts.name: Definition and status of autonomous entities
u: Within certain States, autonomous entities are constituted in order to guarantee the cultural, educational and municipal rights of minority communities.
Autonomous entities hold their own competences in matters of:
education in the minority language and adapted school curricula;
cultural institutions, media and community libraries;
management of ordinary municipal affairs within their territorial perimeter;
preservation and promotion of the cultural and religious heritage of the community;
cross-border cooperation with kindred communities in neighbouring States.

Autonomous entities have no legislative power of their own. They exercise their competences within the framework of the laws of the State to which they are attached and of the Confederal Constitution.
Autonomous entities have a right to be consulted on any decision of the State that directly affects the interests of their community.

arts.name: Protection of autonomous entities
u: The territorial limits of an autonomous entity may not be altered without the consent of the majority of its inhabitants expressed by referendum.
Every State is bound to consult the autonomous entities it hosts before adopting measures that directly affect the education, culture or municipal organisation of their communities.
Autonomous entities may address petitions directly to the Narodni Sabor when they consider that their rights are threatened.
The Confederation ensures respect for the rights of autonomous entities and may intervene in the event of a proven violation.

arts.name: Confederal autonomous municipalities
u: The confederal autonomous municipalities of Brčko and Mostar are directly under confederal jurisdiction. They are attached to no State.
They have a municipal council elected by direct suffrage of their inhabitants.
The composition of their municipal council guarantees fair representation of all resident communities.
The Confederation finances their essential public services.
Their status may be amended only by an amendment to the Constitution, approved in addition by a local referendum.

arts.name: Council of Communities
u: The Council of Communities (Veće Zajednica) represents before the confederal institutions the communities which belong to no constituent people and have autonomous entities: the Albanian, Hungarian, Slovak and Turkish communities.
Its members are appointed by the autonomous entities of each community, as provided by law. Each community holds an equal number of seats.

The Council of Communities gives an opinion on any confederal bill concerning the status of autonomous entities, the languages of their communities or education in those languages. The Kongres and the Narodni Sabor take note of that opinion before deciding.
It may bring disputes concerning the rights of autonomous entities before the Ustavni Sud (Article 118 d).
